The Naturals #4

Sânge rău

Jennifer Lynn Barnes, Bogdan Voiculescu (Translator)

4.37
195,504 ratings25,514 reviews
Rate this book
Noi victime. Noi trădări. Noi secrete.

Când Cassie Hobbes s-a alăturat programului FBI Înzestrații, a avut un singur scop, și anume să elucideze misterul morții mamei sale. Dar după întâmplările din Las Vegas, a ieșit la iveală un adevăr șocant: mama ei trăiește, iar oamenii care o țin captivă sunt mai puternici – și mai periculoși – decât toți adversarii cu care s-au confruntat Înzestrații până acum.

În timp ce Cassie și echipa lucrează contracronometru pentru a descoperi secretele unui grup care a ucis vreme de generații, numărul victimelor crește.

Se pare că, de data asta, situația s-a schimbat.
Înzestrații nu doar că vânează criminali în serie.
Acum ei sunt cei vânați.

About the author

Jennifer Lynn Barnes

58 books63.6k followers
Jennifer Lynn Barnes (who mostly goes by Jen) was born in Tulsa, Oklahoma. She has been, in turn, a competitive cheerleader, a volleyball player, a dancer, a debutante, a primate cognition researcher, a teen model, a comic book geek, and a lemur aficionado. She's been writing for as long as she can remember, finished her first full book (which she now refers to as a "practice book" and which none of you will ever see) when she was still in high school, and then wrote Golden the summer after her freshman year in college, when she was nineteen.

Jen graduated high school in 2002, and from Yale University with a degree in cognitive science (the study of the brain and thought) in May of 2006. She'll be spending the 2006-2007 school year abroad, doing autism research at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

★ 4 stars

𝅄 𓂃 𖥻 “Sometimes, the most dangerous people were the ones you trusted most.” 𑇛 ˚


after thoroughly enjoying the first three installments in The Naturals series and seeing how it kept improving with each book, i couldn’t help but look forward to this last installment and see what the author had in store for us. i had sky-high expectations for this book and i’m very happy to say that those expectations, for the most part, were met.

i’ve been saying since the first book that the author knows how to deliver stories that are unputdownable and just super easy to binge — and this one? this one is no different. i was hooked from beginning to the end. well, how could i not? Bad Blood is intriguing, thrilling and absolutely addictive. it truly has everything to hold your attention. trust me when i say this.

i genuinely think this is the wildest book in the entire series. things got darker and way more intense here, which was kind of expected after the previous book showed us the direction where the story was going, but still... i don’t think i was fully ready for some things that happened. when you compare this plot with the first book’s per example, you can definitely see the drastic difference. i mean, sure, the first book can be considered wild in some ways — but it’s not in the same level. not at all. it’s not a bad thing, though; the story has evolved significantly more and i really liked to see that (even if it made me feel a little scared and disturbed at certain times).

so many things about this book were enjoyable. the plot as a whole, the development of the characters, the found family aspect, the perfect pacing, the short but engaging chapters... but you know what i loved the *most*? the twists & turns and the suspense aspect.

if i had to pick a book in the series that had the best plot twists and the most engaging suspense, i would definitely choose this one. i was on the edge of my seat and biting my nails more times than i can count. everything was so intense and unpredictable — whenever i thought that i figured things out, the author would throw something unexpected [and insane!] and prove me wrong. it made for such an exciting experience.

however, even with all its strengths, i sadly can’t give this book a glowing five star rating. something about the ending just left me... a bit unsatisfied. see, i’m not saying it was bad, but it was definitely rushed, which i wasn’t a big fan of. i needed more details, more time to sit with everything that had happened, and a deeper exploration of specific events that happened. i genuinely believe this book could’ve benefited from more chapters. again, it was not a bad ending, i just wanted more than what was given and didn’t like how abrupt things felt.

all that being said, Bad Blood, in general, still delivers a good conclusion to a series that has been nothing but extremely captivating from the very beginning. JLB did an awesome job and she undoubtedly deserves praise for it.

this entire series has been such a fun ride. i won’t lie that my heart is broken to say goodbye to those characters and this universe... i’m really going to miss it. farewell, The Naturals.

↳˗ˏˋ𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚝ˊˎ˗ ↴:


Cassie has a gift, she is able to make psychological profiles of people just by seeing how they behave, how they dress or how they move. One day she is recruited by the FBI to be part of the Naturals, a group of teenagers, who, like her, have a gift, for solving cold cases. But when a murderer begins to act in a way similar to her mother's murder case, Cassie and the rest of the Naturals' world will turn upside down.

↳˗ˏˋ𝚙𝚊𝚌𝚎 𝚊𝚗𝚍 𝚠𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚒𝚗𝚐ˊˎ˗ ↴:


The pace of the book is very fast, things are happening all the time, and the author's writing is very fast and simple. The chapters are very short, which makes it easy to read.


↳˗ˏˋ𝚏𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚕 𝚝𝚑𝚘𝚞𝚐𝚑𝚝𝚜 ˊˎ˗ ↴:

But, I would still recommend the series 100%, because for a early 2010’s, teenager drama with a love triangle trope, this is fire.

𝑻𝒓𝒐𝒑𝒆𝒔:
📁👤Found Family
👮🏼🔪Murder Mystery x Thriller

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Overview: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

This book had me hooked from start to finish. I loved it so much, and I was on the edge of my seat the entire time, waiting for the twists to be revealed and wondering who would die. I am so glad I gave this series a try after hating The Inheritance Games, because I didn’t expect to love this series as much as I do, nor did I expect to get this attached to these characters.

⁀જ➣꒰ ⋮ ρℓσт.꒱

The plot twists were jaw-dropping, and the author is so smart for pulling them off, because they never crossed my mind. I adore the found family in this series so much. However, I will say that I needed more from that ending. I felt like more needed to be said about the Masters and her mom, but I love the series, which is why I won’t rate this book any less than it deserves.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ 𝕽𝖔𝖒𝖆𝖓𝖈𝖊.꒱

We don’t get much romance in this book, as it was very plot-focused. I would say the romance in this book is very little compared to the rest, but I still enjoyed the bits of romance we got in this book.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ ᭙𝕣ⅈ𝕥ⅈꪀᧁ.꒱

As usual, the writing is very easy to get through.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Characters: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

જ⁀➴ Cassie: Not gonna lie, I don’t care about her mother at all. I actually hate her mother. I’ve struggled to connect with Cassie the way I would prefer with the main character, but oh well, I don’t care about her either. However, she has been through A LOT, to say the least. She is determined to help others, no matter what obstacles come her way.

જ⁀➴ Dean and Micheal: I love them both so much. I'm still Team Dean, and that love confession? It tugged on my heartstrings. I love how supportive Dean is, and how he knows what’s the right thing to say to Cassie. He did piss me off at one point during the book, when he fought with Michael, but glad to see his feelings changing towards Michael. I also adore Michael, but I don’t ship him with Lia AT ALL.

જ⁀➴ Sloane and Lia: Sloane is sometimes...clueless when it comes to things that are not math-related, but I still adore her. You get to see some warmth from Lia, but I’m still indifferent about her—pretty neutral. I don’t love her, but I also don’t hate her.

જ⁀➴ Briggs, Veronica, and Judd: I love them with my entire heart. I need to see Ronnie and Briggs’ wedding ASAP!

જ⁀➴ Celine: I don’t like her at all. Sure, she helped for, like, two times, but other than that—she’s very useless. I don’t like it when any additions happen to a specific group, so she felt unnecessary to me.

── .✦ 𝓕𝓲𝓷𝓪𝓵 𝓣𝓱𝓸𝓾𝓰𝓱𝓽𝓼: I love this series, and these characters so much.

3.5 ⭐️

this book was just… okay. not terrible, but it didn’t give me that finale feeling i was hoping for. the pacing dragged in spots, and the case didn’t hold my attention like earlier ones. i wanted a little more from the story itself, but the characters? they carried.

cassie has been through so much and still managed to push forward. i’ve loved watching her journey throughout the series — she’s determined, sharp, and full of heart, even when she’s hanging on by a thread.

dean was so solid in this one. i loved how steady and supportive he was, especially with cassie. he never tried to fix her, just stood beside her through it all. we love a quiet, loyal king.

michael was really strong in this book. his loyalty to the group was clear, and even when things got messy, he kept showing up. his dynamic with cassie felt more grounded this time around, and i really liked how his character was handled overall.

sloane owns my heart. she’s clever, observant, and her loyalty to the group never wavers. every time she spoke, i was either smiling or emotional — she’s so underrated and so special.

lia really impressed me in this one. she had some standout moments, and her growth was subtle but noticeable. her sharpness was still there, but we got to see more warmth underneath.

"𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘪𝘴𝘯’𝘵 𝘢 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘤𝘦. 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘦𝘰𝘱𝘭𝘦 𝘸𝘩𝘰 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦 𝘺𝘰𝘶. 𝘍𝘰𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳, 𝘯𝘰 𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘸𝘩𝘢𝘵."





I loved this book and truly enjoyed the entire ride. The case was so complex I couldn’t suspect anyone — they were all too obvious or too far off. I just had to wait till the end and feel the chaos unfold 😮‍💨

What I really appreciated was how this book gave us more of Michael early on, and then focused on Lia later — both of them were so powerful in their own way. Also, I surprisingly loved Celine! Her abilities were actually so useful in this one.
Cassie felt a bit selfish at the beginning, but hey, she’s still a teen with a ton on her shoulders.
Sloane? Brilliant and hilarious as always — the brain of the team and also the accidental comic relief 😭
And Dean finally started reacting to Michael’s teasing?? That was comedy gold 😂
Lia’s jealousy moments? Top-tier drama. Loved it. Their teenage energy was chaotic, messy, and so real — exactly what I came for.

Also, is it just me or did everyone in this series discover a secret sibling? 😂 I kept waiting for it to happen to Dean too… but let’s be real — with his father? Yeah, no way 😅

And can we talk about Briggs and Sterling for a second?? I’ve loved them since book one — they’re amazing together. I’m glad Briggs didn’t lose his edge, but seriously, those two better get remarried already 😤

The ending was bittersweet. Cassie’s story closed on a sad but meaningful note... Her idea of forming a team of Naturals hit hard. It honestly gave Marvel vibes — like she’s assembling a new generation of superpowered misfits. This NEEDS to be a TV series.❤️✨

In the end, I’m so glad I decided to continue the series. Funny how I almost stopped after book one back in March 😅 Now I’m already missing the whole crew. I’ll definitely read the novella — I’m not ready to let go just yet 💔



Here we go… final book. I’m not ready 😭❤️

unpopular opinion time

this may sound picky of me because it is but this was a solid 3.75. making it ... drumroll please ... my least favorite in the series!!

look, this wasn’t bad. i enjoyed it, it was entertaining, and it was the classic jlb fast-paced-short-chapters-ya-mystery i was looking for. the cast of characters is one of my favorites, ever.

HOWEVER

this dragged on WAY. TOO. MUCH. it wasn’t even that long - 373 pages - but it felt like 600. it literally felt like nothing happened until the last 50 pages (i’m aware this isn’t factual but it’s how it seemed).

it also doesn’t help that cassie is my least favorite character (is this controversial?), and the whole plot centered around her. i was very a little disappointed that we didn’t get more of lia’s story. quite honestly, i could not have cared less about cassie and her past!

my main problem with this, though, is the plot. i knew at the end of all in that i most likely wasn’t going to love this one, because i didn’t like the hint of the plot that we got then. for some reason the whole cult thing just didn’t appeal to me? add to that the fact that i was straight up confused for a good portion - not the best combination.

i will miss the series though! i adore these characters and the found family here, and the epilogue in this made my heart so happy. i wish we could’ve gotten more of celine, but u know. saving twelve for a day i long for these characters again.

⋅˚₊‧ ୨ my thoughts ୧ ‧₊˚ ⋅

Jennifer Lynn Barnes has done it again. honestly, she's a mastermind. I love how she gives us these little hints throughout a book, and it all falls perfectly in a place at the end. this series is the best one written by JLB (sorry tig, love you too) it managed to keep me entertained and invested all the way through. and the case that the naturals were working on in bad blood was my personal favorite! it was so interesting and intriguing on its own way, and I got so immersed in the story that it was literally impossible to put it down. it had me totally in a chokehold. furthermore, bad blood was such a good conclusion to this series, and I absolutely loved how the loose ends got tied up. I'll definitely miss this series and these wonderful characters so much 🥹

⋅˚₊‧ ୨ characters ୧ ‧₊˚ ⋅

ᝰ.ᐟ Cassie Hobbes

she's an amazing fmc. a very likeable one! the amount of pain she goes through every time is insane. and you don't know how bad I felt for her throughout the entire book. she experienced so much AGAIN, and she didn't deserve none of this. tho, I'm happy for her that she finally got the answers to her questions. I adored the friendship that has been formed between Cassie and Lia, they are such a good duo!
✧₊⁺ "and I use knowing things about people as an excause to keep them from knowing me."
ᝰ.ᐟ Dean Redding

our golden boy. he hasn't healed from his trauma yet and probably never fully will. he struggles with so many problems of his own, and constantly fights his demons, and yet he's so supportive and caring when it comes to his friends. the way he was there for Cassie when she needed him, and the way he comforted her 🥹 his friendship with Lia is so adorable.
✧₊⁺ "I love you. Today, tomorrow, covered in blood, haunted and waking up in the middle of the night screaming — I love you, Cassie, and I'm here, and I'm not going anywhere."
ᝰ.ᐟ Sloane Tavish

our coffeine addicted girl, a ray of sunshine in other people's darkness. her obsession with numbers and statistics is what makes her so unique. honestly, I don't know what she's talking about for like most of the time, but she's such a lil nerd and I adore her for it. the naturals became to her a family she's never had. and also her friendship with Michael is so heartwarming and precious. ❤️‍🩹
✧₊⁺ "Are you okay?" Michael asked Sloane.
Sloane took three tiny, hesitant steps, then threw herself at Michael, latching her arms around his neck so tightly that I wasn’t sure she would ever let go.

✧₊⁺ "I thought you were fundamentally opposed to giving Sloane caffeine."
"I am. Most of the time. But you know what the song says: it's my three-day-long party, and I'll caffeinate my Sloane if I want to."
ᝰ.ᐟ Michael Townsend

hear me out: Dean is perfect for Cassie, but Michael is a better character.

his backstory is truly heartbreaking. if Thatcher Townsend has no haters then I'm dead. Michael himself has developed a lot throughout the entire series, and even though sometimes the things he says don't sit right with me (why on earth would he say this to Lia? 🥲), I still adore him. he's so funny, and always knows how to lighten up the atmosphere when it's clearly needed. him and Dean were genuinely hilarious in this one. I mean, yay, a miracle happened and Michael has grown on Dean! they're definitely besties now
✧₊⁺ "Do you like me?"
"You have your moments."
"What was that?"
"I don't have to like you. We're family."
"Bossom buddies."
ᝰ.ᐟ Lia Zhang
I wasn't the biggest fan of her in the previous books. she was pretty annoying, and at times she was just getting on my nerves. tho, with time she has definitely grown on me. she opened up a lot about her past, which helped me understand her so much better. Lia's backstory is terribly sad. nobody should go through something like this at such a young age. but due to her experiences she's incredibly strong now.
✧₊⁺ "I love you, Sadie."
It would be easier, for Lia, if that were a lie.

✧₊⁺ "I forgot what it was like to be special one moment and nothing the next."

⠀ ── ⋆˙⟡ ⠀

౿꒰ 🕯️ ⌗ my thoughts
well. okay. so i really did enjoy this. but! i have feelings. and i’m still figuring out what to do with them. this series has been such a fun time and this book gave a lot of what i wanted. but also? not everything. and i think that’s where i’m stuck.

first off? i’m sad. last book. end of the naturals. it’s weird because i waited literal years to start this series and now it’s already over?? but this was still good. it had the same vibe i’ve grown attached to. and the last 20%?? insane. that part delivered.

the rest of it… i don’t know. it’s not that anything was bad, but the structure felt kinda strange. like half the book is about something totally different before we even get to the plot we’ve been waiting for. and then when the big reveals do come, they’re somehow both shocking and not shocking at all? like yes, some things were absolutely wild. but others landed more like, “omg what?? okay anyway!” and then we’d just move on. i think that’s where the weirdness came from. this is the finale. the buildup has been four books long. so even though i liked where it went, i kept expecting a little more.

but! i still liked this a lot. i don’t know if i’m totally satisfied with this as the ending, but i’m really glad i read this series. it was such a good time.


౿꒰ 🗝️ ⌗ characters
⟡ cassandra “cassie” hobbes.
her memory is so bad it’s actually kinda relatable. she’s still going through it but she’s trying her best. i’m glad she got to wrap up her story even if the closure felt a little quick.

⟡ dean redding.
he was great. he’s always great. and he continues to be the most normal person in the house while also having the worst backstory. like he’s just chill. i genuinely don’t have more to say because he never misses.

⟡ michael townsend.
he was not okay this book. and i get it! he was going through it. but some of his choices?? yeah… didn’t love. i still think he’s a really strong character, though. also. the celine stuff especially was… not great.

⟡ lia zhang + sloane tavish.
lia might’ve actually been my favorite this time? i liked her in the last book but she was great here. it took me like two books to warm up to her but i do like her now. sloane was great too (as always) and i lowkey wish we got more of her with celine. there was so much potential there and we barely got anything.


౿꒰ 🔗 ⌗ romance
very background this time around. which isn’t unusual for this series, but it was definitely even less present here. the dynamic is still there and still feels nice, but romance wasn’t the focus at all. not mad about it! just kinda wished for one moment near the end to wrap it up better.


౿꒰ 🧿 ⌗ extras
⊹ sloane and the blowtorch.
⊹ creepy little interludes from the killer’s pov will always work.
⊹ sloane and celine deserved a whole subplot.


౿꒰ ⚖️ ⌗ overall
as a series finale… i’m still kinda undecided on it. but as a book? this was such a good time. wild, unhinged, and full of insane shit. this series has been a favorite and even though i wanted more from the ending, i’m really glad i read it all the way through.
